title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: one-man-in-Adam reply; whence from Scripture?
pass_a_gloss: Now your answer. You say those born of Adam are viewed as one man in him, that all sinned in him, and that his first actually committed sin is charged and ascribed to them so that they count as sinners sentenced to death. May I press the source—Scripture, or something else? Who is to view all as one man if not God? How did you learn of that inward act of the divine mind? The text is silent, and reason pushes back.
pass_b_english: But let us hear your answer. I answer, you say, that all men born from Adam are considered as one man in Adam, and all sinned in him, so that the first sin which he actually committed is imputed and ascribed to them, and it is enough that they be held for sinners and adjudged to death. May I ask whence you have that—from Scripture, or elsewhere? For by whom do you want all men to be considered as one man, if not by God? Whence, then, did that inner act of the divine mind become known to you? Scripture is silent; reason protests.
source_text: Sed tuam responsionem audiamus. Respondeo, inquis, omnes homines ex Adamo natos considerari tanquam unum hominem in Adamo & omnes peccasse in illo, ita ut primum peccatum, quod actualiter commisit, illis imputetur, & tribuatur, & satis sit ut habeantur pro peccatoribus, & morti adjudicentur. Licetne mihi quaerere, unde id habeas, ex Scriptura, an aliunde? nam a quo vis considerari omnes homines tanquam unum hominem, nisi a Deo? Unde igitur tibi iste mentis divinae internus actus innotuit? Tacet Scriptura, reclamat ratio.
